description: This horizontal bar chart, titled “Criterion” on the vertical axis and “Number of Participants” on the horizontal axis, illustrates the number of participants who rated each criterion on a scale from 0 to 6. The vertical axis lists seven criteria in descending order of participant count: “Relevant FCs” (6 participants), “FC Summary” (5 participants), “Relevance Explanation” (3 participants), “Clarity and Simplicity” (3 participants), “Overall Summary” (2 participants), “Filters” (1 participant), and “Veracity Explanation” (1 participant). Each criterion is represented by a colored bar extending horizontally from left to right, with the bar length corresponding to the number of participants, and the exact value is labeled at the end of each bar. The bars are colored differently for distinction: “Relevant FCs” is dark purple, “FC Summary” is dark teal, “Relevance Explanation” is medium teal, “Clarity and Simplicity” is greenish-teal, “Overall Summary” is green, “Filters” is light green, and “Veracity Explanation” is yellow-green. The horizontal axis is linear, scaled from 0 to 6, with tick marks at intervals of 2. The chart does not show any grouping or stacking of bars; each criterion has its own individual bar. The bars are sorted in descending order by participant count, with the highest value (“Relevant FCs” with 6) at the top and the lowest values (“Filters” and “Veracity Explanation” with 1) at the bottom. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, or outlines beyond their standard presentation.
